sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup, output folder, and colour palette
sections.what: Sets the output folder from the command line and defines the named colours that each material uses.
sections.why: The docstring says material names match the keys the viewer understands, so the palette must use those names.
sections.watch_out: Every material name used by an element must have a palette entry, or building that element fails.

sections.name: material
sections.title: Creating named materials
sections.what: Gets an existing material with the given name, or creates one with the palette colour.
sections.why: Keeps one material per name, so the viewer can recolour by name.
sections.watch_out: A name missing from the palette causes an error.

sections.name: _finish
sections.title: Attaching a material and queuing a part
sections.what: Adds a material to a shape and adds the shape to the list of parts that will be joined and exported.
sections.why: Every part must be queued this way or it will be left out of the exported model.
sections.watch_out: Forgetting to call this for a new part silently drops it from the export.

sections.name: box
sections.title: Rectangular block
sections.what: Creates a box of a given size, location, and optional rotation.
sections.why: Boxes are the most common building block for walls, slabs, and equipment.
sections.watch_out: The size is the full length, width, and height, not half of each.

sections.name: cyl
sections.title: Cylinder or cone
sections.what: Creates a cylinder, or a cone when a top radius is given.
sections.why: Used for tanks, pipes, columns, and rounded supports.
sections.watch_out: Passing a top radius switches the shape to a cone, which is easy to miss.

sections.name: sphere
sections.title: Sphere
sections.what: Creates a ball shape, optionally stretched along one or more axes.
sections.why: Used for rounded ends such as the top of a process column.
sections.watch_out: The stretch values change the shape but not the radius, so sizes can be misread.

sections.name: torus
sections.title: Ring
sections.what: Creates a doughnut-shaped ring with a set major and minor radius.
sections.why: Used for bands, flanges, and rings on tanks and towers.
sections.watch_out: The major radius is the distance to the ring centre, so it must be larger than the minor radius.

sections.name: beam
sections.title: Square structural bar
sections.what: Creates a square bar between two points, rotated to point along the line between them.
sections.why: Used for steel members in frames and towers.
sections.watch_out: Two identical points would create a zero-length bar, which can break the rotation calculation.

sections.name: pyramid
sections.title: Four-sided roof or mound
sections.what: Creates a four-sided pyramid shape with a rectangular base, used for hip roofs and ballast mounds.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the docstring description.
sections.watch_out: It applies the rotation with a Blender operation that needs a particular context, so changing the call order can fail.

sections.name: from_points
sections.title: Custom mesh from points
sections.what: Builds a mesh from a given list of points and faces, then queues it as a part.
sections.why: Used when a standard shape is not enough, such as the sloped shapes in the building and bridge elements.
sections.watch_out: Each face must refer only to points that exist in the list, or the mesh is broken.

sections.name: prism
sections.title: Extruded profile
sections.what: Extends a flat two-dimensional outline along the X axis to make a long solid, such as a dam wall cross-section.
sections.why: The docstring says it is used for dam and breakwater cross-sections.
sections.watch_out: The outline must be a closed loop, or the faces will not close.

sections.name: arch
sections.title: Arched outline
sections.what: Computes a curved outline for a barrel vault roof, spanning a given half width and rise.
sections.why: Used to make the curved roof of a building or hangar.
sections.watch_out: The step count controls smoothness, so a low value gives a visibly faceted roof.

sections.name: tube
sections.title: Hollow tube
sections.what: Builds a hollow cylinder along the X axis, with an outer and inner radius, for tunnel linings and walls.
sections.why: The docstring says it is used for tunnel linings and ring walls.
sections.watch_out: The face direction flags decide whether the inside or outside faces out. A wrong flag makes the tube look inside out.

sections.name: ring_wall
sections.title: Upright hollow wall
sections.what: Makes a hollow upright cylinder by turning a tube upright and moving it into place.
sections.why: Used for basin and tank walls.
sections.watch_out: It depends on the tube's axis direction, so a change to the tube function changes this shape.

sections.name: export
sections.title: Joining and exporting one element
sections.what: Applies any turn to the queued parts, joins them into one mesh, exports a GLB file, records the native size in viewer axes, and removes the temporary object.
sections.why: Likely reason: each element becomes one file the viewer can load, and the native size is needed for scaling.
sections.watch_out: The turn value is removed from the entry it was given, and the export fails if no parts were queued. The size order uses viewer axes, which differ from Blender's order.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Main program that builds and exports all models
sections.what: Clears the open Blender scene, then builds every model in BUILDERS, exports each one, writes a manifest.json listing them and prints how many were exported. The main call at the bottom runs whenever this file is run.
sections.why: Likely reason: clearing the scene first ensures each run starts from a clean slate.
sections.watch_out: The first step removes everything in the open Blender session, so any unsaved work in that session will be lost.

summary: A Blender script that builds detailed 3D models of common facility elements, such as turbines, tanks, bridges, and conveyors, and exports each as one GLB file with a manifest entry.
purpose: Produces the library of 3D element models that the viewer can show and recolour.
why: The docstring states the goal: named materials that the viewer understands, with representative proportions in metres rather than vendor drawings.
how: Run inside Blender without a window, the script defines materials and simple shapes, then builds each element from those shapes. The export step joins the parts, writes one GLB file, and records the element's native size in the manifest.
inputs: An output folder after a double dash on the command line, and Blender's built-in bpy library. Only 31 of 73 sections were supplied.
outputs: One GLB file per element and a manifest entry with the native size. The code that writes the manifest file is not in the supplied sections.
risks: The script only runs inside Blender. Materials must match the palette names exactly. The docstring names scripts/build_model_library.py, but this file is named build_library.py, so the run command in the docstring may be wrong.
debug: If bpy cannot be imported, run the script through Blender. If a material key error appears, the palette is missing that name. If a model looks inside out or sideways, check the face order and the axis conversion in the export step.
